title: Leo fell through the ice 🧊
lines: Leo fell through the ice.
December. Leo took the shortcut across the pond.
@af_heart: "Leo, stop! It's too thin!"
Crack. Then black, freezing water.
First comes cold shock. You gasp, and your breathing runs wild.
@am_michael: "Leo! Slow your breathing!"
Cold-water experts call it one, ten, one.
One [minute](minnit) to calm your breathing. Ten minutes to get out. About an hour before you pass out.
@af_heart: "Turn back the way you came! That ice held you!"
Arms flat on the ice. Kick your legs up behind you.
Slide out on your belly. Don't stand up. Roll away.
He made it. Shaking, but alive.
@am_echo: "How thin was it?"
@af_heart: "Under four inches of new, clear ice? Stay off."
@am_echo: "Was anyone ever trapped under the ice?"
@af_heart: "Yes. For eighty minutes."
May [1999](nineteen ninety-nine), Norway. Skier Anna [Bågenholm](Bawgun-hollm) fell head-first through a frozen stream.
She found an air pocket and stayed conscious about forty minutes. Then her heart stopped.
Rescuers pulled her out after eighty minutes.
Her body was down to [13.7](thirteen point seven) degrees Celsius. Normal is thirty-seven.
Over a hundred doctors and nurses worked nine hours, warming her blood in a heart-lung machine.
She lived, and became a radiologist at the hospital that saved her.
@am_michael: "Okay. We're taking the long way."
Because the shortcut is how Leo fell through the ice.
